column8: Wed 18 Nov: store only; the current Navy rule (ballpoint, no fair copy) corrects claim 1, but a log binds by being written at the time and signed, the reading the definition keeps out (Q42), so never a turn.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q79-019 (no erasures, a single line kept legible) with the current instruction; the record closes on the commanding officer's signature, the signed sense, so store only.

Wed 18 Nov: a writers' method note for 3.0 and 3a, never a turn: each inking keeps its own date, so the top-up ($2,388 in January 2028 money, NUMBERS) and the extra Treasuries are January 2028 purchases; CONCEIT s3 already holds the rule, and a log is a signed record.

Wed 18 Nov: refuse for the report, the card's kill stands: rough to smooth is a draft made final by copying, which maps ink to decided and points pencil at the IPS (V2.4 guard 3); store as the recorded disanalogy.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q44-014 (pencils first, erased once inked) on a ship's slate; adds no plan step, and the medium is CONFLICTING (slate or paper).

Wed 18 Nov: store for CONCEIT s8 only, and fix the mapping first: a fund swap replaces the ended or merged fund (Table 3 row 4), so never a purchase beside the old or the ten bought in January 2027 all stay; a signed log, never a turn; 1981 regulations read as made, amendments unchecked.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q79-019 (entries at the time of the occurrence, signed); tautological for logs, which record only what has happened, and signed, so no turn.

Wed 18 Nov: writers' guard for 2.0: in surveying the legal record must be pencil (FM 6-2), so the medium binds nothing and the conceit rightly defines ink by owning (V2.1); never beside Laura's pencil, which waits where the surveyor's lasts; read on a mirror (globalsecurity), edition undated.
Wed 18 Nov: the plainest wording of row 8's kill (pencil to stop smearing, admitted in court); a teaching text, so row 8's Army rule leads.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: the original, not the neat copy, is the record, and later additions carry their own date (joins row 3); a measurement record, read in extracts only.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: the BLM's inking step is a transcription for the archive, and filing, not ink, binds (row 12); no plan step.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q79-004 (a record counts from an act on a public register, not from its writing); filing by an authorised official pulls toward signed off, so never for Laura's figures.

Wed 18 Nov: store behind Q79-004 for 2.0: the surveyed line becomes unchangeable when title passes, ownership fixing the record; never a third land turn (Q79-004, Q79-036), and the line is fixed to protect a new owner, not because its maker owns.
Wed 18 Nov: context and reference for rows 15-16: the smooth sheet is NOAA's official permanent record, so pencil and ink sit on one record others rely on; never staged.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, a fact behind the verb inked in January 2028 (a line waits in pencil until the work it depends on is done, then is inked); closer to pencil and ink than Q121-028's woodblock, so one or the other behind the verb, never both; say completed, never verified or approved, since NOAA's ink also follows a review board's approval (row 17), the signed-off sense.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 15 (each pencil line inked once its condition is met, so one record carries lines with different inking dates); its trigger is verification, nearer signed off than row 15's completion.

Wed 18 Nov: refuse for the report: ink after a review board's approval is the signed-off reading the definition keeps out (Q42); store as the recorded disanalogy and the reason rows 15-16 say completed, never approved.
Wed 18 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: names are inked once approved, and her flexibility is never inked; recorded so no one re-proposes it.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q114-021 (the models as pencil beside the record) and Q79-018 (fix against dead reckoning); a navigator's working lines are a trade image, the archives' rule needs no trade word, so Q114-021 leads.
Wed 18 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: ink on a graphite base is a second staged trade image (rounds 6-8 failed every one), and why no top is stated before the move is NUMBERS 4's, said plainly.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3b-3c: the chart keeps the shoaler of two figures, the form of 2033's rule, the lower of what the funds pay and the top she stated (CONCEIT s3); the chart takes the lower for the reader's safety, Laura's is a cap with the excess hers, so never beside row 22 in prose.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b, the exact craft fact behind every end is rounded down: by international rule (IHO S-4 B-412, 2026, read at source) every printed depth goes to the safe side, as the unrounded $117,142 is stated $115,000 and $97,605 is $95,000 (NUMBERS); one clause, read cold with the definition first; say the safe side (row 24), never conservative or prudent (WORDS).
Wed 18 Nov: 3c store: IHO rounds so the printed precision never misleads; NUMBERS's reason for rounding down is the margin, not precision, so say it fits, never that it is why the rule rounds.
Wed 18 Nov: the guard on row 22 (drying heights round up, clearances down): the rule is the side the reader relies on, so say the safe side, never always round down; carried in row 22's note.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b-3c store: B-417's warning against too much caution fits the two-sided cost (rounding each part would give $110,000, WORDS, the difference going to her flexibility), but it is a parallel, never the reason the rule rounds once and holds back only 0.5% (NUMBERS: bond reader 3's arithmetic); the card's judge's note says which is why and must change.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.0, behind the word ink only: one source inks the chart and any other may be noted in pencil, as ink comes only from a Treasury she owns paying on its date and every forecast, share price or unpaid deposit is pencil; never the reason for one issuer (round 5; IPS l.11's matching rule), and the source is an authority, so never staged; NP100 read in a c.2009 reproduction, current wording unread.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c and 3.0, the strongest conceit fact on the card: an approved harbour work stays in pencil until it is finished, then is inked, so pencil means not yet there, not undecided, the answer CONCEIT V2.5 lacked to the law's deliberative pencil (Q114); behind inked before the 2031 meetings (the move fixed by IPS l.15), never staged; gloss with the definition's words, never not yet owned for VT; read the current NP100 or NP294 before citing.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3e: rubbing out temporary notices leaves the chart current for every permanent one, a fact outside comics for erase every pencil line now that Adams is refused (Q114-001, contra the card); Martin already carries 3e's turn, so store; fails for her flexibility (pencil because it lapses), as the card records.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Richmond (Q44-011) and the ledger (Q106): chart ink is crossed through, never erased; nothing new for the plan.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.0 or 3d, a writers' fact for the rule itself: the chart's correction note is written only once the correction is applied, and not before, as Laura names a figure only once she owns it; one clause at most, never in her words (guard 4), and kept to the timing, since a record entry leans toward signing.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, behind the printed page only: the chart the office issues carries permanent notices and leaves temporary ones to the user's pencil, so the printed page shows only ink outside comics too; 3d's turn needs no second field and puts no word in Laura's lines, so store.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 22 (a chart never shows more water than there is) and of Q79-024 (golf's overstated score); row 22's rounding rule is the plainer fact, one of them at most.
Wed 18 Nov: store context: the older NOAA rule rounded some depths up, so always to the safe side is the modern, stricter rule; no part.
Wed 18 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: lab ink means dated and unaltered and inks plans too, so beside Laura it would ink the 2031 move before it is made (IPS l.15); read in extracts only.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q79-018 (every figure carries its kind, modelled or owned) in a weaker field; the report's we modelled already does it.

Wed 18 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: a theatre plays to its audience from pencil and fixes the book after opening, the order inverted from Laura's; store as Q79-034's recorded disanalogy, never pointed at the IPS (guard 3).

Wed 18 Nov: for the lead: across six fields only charts make ink depend on its source and mean in force now, with pencil for decided but not yet there, the line that matches Laura's; a Keel synthesis, so cite rows 22, 26 and 27, never this row.

Wed 18 Nov: placement map for the lead, right in shape (facts behind working words, none staged, no new turn); fix two points: row 15 or Q121-028 behind the verb, never both, and Adams is refused (Q114-001), so row 28 is the non-comics fact for 3e if one is wanted.
